why: The answer is the longest run of one repeated character. A window that grows while the character stays the same and restarts when it changes finds every run in one pass.
hints: Every candidate substring is one maximal run of the same letter.
Scan left to right with a run length that grows while the letter repeats and resets to 1 when it changes; that is a window whose left edge jumps to the change point.
Keep the best letter and length, updating on >= so a later run of equal length replaces an earlier one. Return letter + str(length). O(n).
pitfalls: Ties go to the rightmost run: compare with >=, not >.
The output joins the letter and the count as text, e.g. 'c3', and the count can have two or more digits ('a100').
A one-character string returns that letter + '1'.
